Albayzin ferry Review

Review of Albayzin ferry

MV Albayzin ferry is a Ro-Ro passenger vessel operated by the Spanish company TRASMEDITERRANEA. The ship has a maximum capacity of 949 passengers and 172 cars. Launched in 2004, the vessel currently operates on Spain-Canary Islands ferry routes from Cadiz to the Canaries (Lanzarote, Fuerteventura, Gran Canaria, La Palma, Tenerife), with a crossing time of approximately 40 hours.

Cabins

As a cruise ferry, Albayzin has a total of 400 berths in 2-, 3-, or 4-bed staterooms (inside and outside), all air-conditioned and equipped with en-suite bathrooms. The ferry company provides bed linens, towels, and toiletries. Some staterooms are wheelchair-accessible and adapted for passengers with disabilities.

All passengers must vacate their staterooms 30 minutes prior to arriving at the homeport. Passengers with reduced mobility board the ship first, while those traveling with vehicles disembark last. All Trasmediterranea ships offer reserved seating adapted for passengers with reduced mobility and visual impairments. Common bathrooms onboard are also accessible.

For passengers traveling without a cabin but with reserved seats, the ship provides a dedicated, locked luggage room. The luggage limit is 40 kg (bridge) and 30 kg (seating area).

Shipboard dining and entertainment options

As facilities, the Albayzin ship offers:

  • A la carte Restaurant with a Mediterranean menu featuring fresh-made dishes from locally sourced ingredients. The restaurant includes a wine cellar offering a wide selection of premium wines. Dishes include Iberian ham, fresh salads, crawfish croquettes, meats, seafood, paella, and homemade desserts.
  • Buffet Restaurant (self-service) serving hot and cold dishes, salad bar, rice and pasta dishes, tapas, omelets, soups, stews, meats, and seafood. Beverages include hot and cold drinks, beer, and wine by the glass. Special menus include a Children's Menu, vegetarian options, and healthy meals. Signature meal combos include "Combo Grumete" (spaghetti with Bolognese sauce and soda) and "Combo Neptuno" (hamburger, fries, and soda).
  • The Café is a self-service patisserie and coffee shop offering sandwiches, cakes, pastries, pizzas, snacks (paninis, appetizers), premium chocolates, homemade ice cream, fresh juices, and a variety of beverages.
  • All Trasmediterranea ships offer gluten-free and Moroccan halal food options, such as vegetable tagine, lamb, chicken, and fish dishes.
  • Many onboard services and packages (including dining) can be purchased when booking your Trasmediterranea ferry ticket.
  • Boutiques are duty-free shops offering perfumes, cosmetics, leather goods, children’s items (toys, coloring books), confectionery, clothing, fashion accessories, electronics, travel essentials, gifts, spirits, wines, and tobacco. Promotions are offered regularly. On Spain-Canaries and Spain-Morocco routes, duty-free pricing applies. Exclusive Kukuxumusu products are also available.
  • Kids Play Area includes an indoor supervised playground, ball pool, nursery, changing room, and childcare services. During peak season (June to September), themed activities and workshops for children are organized, including group games, arts and crafts, Pirate Day, and a MiniDisco with clowns and parties.
  • Sun Deck includes a Solarium (outdoor relaxation area with sun loungers) and a pets area (kennels and walking space). Passengers may visit their pets during the voyage, but must request permission for deck walks.
  • Disco Bar offering a selection of drinks
  • Video Games Room (arcade machines and XBOX consoles)
  • Free Wi-Fi and ATM (located next to the Information Desk/Reception)

The top deck is a Heli Deck with a helipad used for emergency helicopter landings.

All public decks are accessible via passenger elevators and connected by staircases.

Emergency instructions are posted in staterooms, displayed on TV screens, and at muster stations. Life jackets are available at assembly stations. Elevators must not be used in emergencies.

Trasmediterranea ferry deals

For foot passengers, boarding closes 30 minutes before departure (15 minutes for fast ferries). Car passengers must board at least 1 hour before departure. Boarding is not permitted after the cutoff time. On Spain-Canaries routes, customs checks require all passengers to arrive at the terminal at least 2 hours in advance.

Boarding cards can be issued online when booking or via self-service kiosks at ferry terminals. All passengers (including infants and pets) must have individual boarding cards. Lost cards are replaced free of charge.

To enter Morocco, passengers must present valid ID cards, passports, and visas (where applicable). All documents must be valid for the duration of the stay.

Pregnant women must sign an "Information Document for Pregnant Travelers." Travel is not allowed for women over 36 weeks pregnant. Babies (0-2 years) travel free but do not receive a lounge seat. Children under 13 must be accompanied by an adult. Children ages 2-13 receive a 50% discount.

Trasmediterranea offers the following discounts:

  • 100% discount for babies (0-2 years); travel free but must be booked in advance and do not receive a seat
  • 50% discount for children (ages 2-13)
  • 50% resident discount (applied to ticket prices)
  • 40-50% military discount (based on agreement with military corps)
  • 20% discount for large families
  • 50% discount for large families with special needs
  • 100% discount for small pets in carriers (travel free)

Combined ferry+bus package deals are also available with discounted pricing across all routes.

Pets on the ship

Pets (birds, cats, dogs, and non-aggressive animals) are allowed onboard with car or foot passengers. They are not permitted on passenger decks. Car passengers may leave pets in their vehicles or use the ship’s kennels. Foot passengers must transport pets in a cage or carrier (max size 50x40x25 cm), which must be used throughout the trip. Large dogs must be leashed and muzzled.

Pet boarding cards are required. Passengers must specify the transport method (cage or carrier) when booking. Pet fares and accommodations vary by route. A valid healthcare card with vaccination and deworming records is required.

Pets travel for a fee in ship kennels or free of charge in carriers. Onboard kennels are parasite-resistant, and cleaned and disinfected before each voyage. A first-aid kit and 24-hour pet support hotline are available. Carriers must have a waterproof bottom and be covered.

Guide and assistance dogs for disabled passengers have full access to all public areas and travel free of charge. They must be leashed, muzzled, and have a veterinarian ID and official tag.

Car decks

Car passengers can travel without baggage limits. All vehicles must have valid documentation and insurance. Vehicle boarding closes 1 hour before departure; late arrivals are not guaranteed boarding. Luggage may be left inside the vehicle, but garage access is closed during the voyage. Ferry car rates vary by route and vehicle size.

Free transport is available for bicycles, surfboards, and sea kayaks, which are secured in the garage.

Car deck safety procedures include:

  • Passengers needing assistance should contact the Information Desk (open 24 hours).
  • Apply the handbrake, engage parking gear, turn off the engine, lights, and electrical equipment. Shut off gas cylinders. Lock the vehicle.
  • Take only valuables and essential hand luggage.
  • Note your vehicle's location and garage deck/stairway number.
  • Access to vehicle decks is prohibited during the voyage.
  • Smoking is not allowed on vehicle decks, in cabins, or lounges.
  • Wait for an onboard announcement before returning to your vehicle.
  • Do not start the engine until instructed to avoid air pollution.

The ship’s operator, Trasmediterranea (fleet), was founded in 1916 and is headquartered in Madrid, Spain. Part of the Acciona Group, the company provides passenger and cargo ferry services between mainland Spain and the Canary Islands, Balearic Islands, and North Africa (Morocco, Algeria).
